column12: a fifth of the untreated pool a year, the rate the ABBV-1480 and volrustomig seeds give a first-line NSCLC entrant against pembrolizumab. The case for it is the randomised phase 2: with chemotherapy, SSGJ-707 at 10 mg/kg gave a confirmed response rate of 58.6% in non-squamous disease against 38.7% for tislelizumab with chemotherapy (abstract 1328), a response rate and not a survival result. It is not first of its class into the line: ivonescimab's HARMONi-3 (NCT05899608) completes in December 2028, two months earlier (the ABBV-1480 seed), and pumitamig against pembrolizumab in PD-L1 of 50% or more (NCT07361510) follows in October 2031 (trials table). The identity carries every eligible patient onto therapy in time: about $10.5bn in the US at the plateau on this indication (of $26.4bn in total), 56% of Keytruda's $18,829mm of US sales in FY2025 across all its indications (asset_revenue_regions), so read it as the ceiling for the class in this line, not a share of it

column12: a fifth of the untreated pool a year. It displaces bevacizumab, which went into 51% of US first-line regimens (Abrams et al., J Natl Cancer Inst 2014, doi:10.1093/jnci/djt371), in a mismatch repair proficient population where PD-1 antibodies have no approved role, so the case rests on the bispecific's VEGF arm beating bevacizumab. It does not read out alone: pumitamig with chemotherapy against bevacizumab with chemotherapy in the same line (NCT07221357) completes in February 2030, a month earlier (trials table). A checkpoint price in a line anchored on a biosimilar argues for less rather than more. The identity carries every eligible patient onto therapy in time: about $4.5bn in the US at the plateau (of $11.2bn in total) at a price bevacizumab has never commanded, so read the plateau as a ceiling

column11: derived: Pfizer generated $23,703mm of free cash flow on $185,759mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 12.76% margin, against the 33.8% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. The 2021 and 2022 COVID years are excluded because a 36% margin on a vaccine windfall is not what this company earns. Restated before interest: PFE paid $8,181mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 4.40% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 22.18% to 17.77%. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Restated without one-off cash: PFE's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $1,350mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $63mm of legal settlements; $4,400mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 1,000mm; 2024 instalment 1,300mm; 2025 instalment 2,100mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 17.77% to 14.52%.
